q: List Revolution's Resolve-style edit commands and their keys.
a:
Each is one undo step and works from the source (the Source monitor's clip with its In and Out), the destination tracks patched in the track headers and the record point (the timeline In mark, otherwise the playhead):
- `edit.insert` (F9) and `edit.overwrite` (F10): three-point Insert and Overwrite.
- `edit.replace` (F11): swaps the clip under the playhead, Source monitor frame lined up with the playhead, same length or shorter if the media runs out.
- `edit.placeOnTop` (F12): overwrites onto the track above the highest one with a clip at the record point, adding a track if needed.
- `edit.append` (Shift+F12): to the end of the timeline.
- `edit.rippleOverwrite` (Shift+F10): swaps the clip under the playhead for the whole source and moves everything after by the difference.
- `edit.fitToFill` (Shift+F11): needs timeline In and Out; changes speed so the marked source fills them.
- Cut page: `edit.smartInsert` (at the clip boundary nearest the playhead), `edit.closeUp` (track above, zoomed to 150%), `edit.sourceOverwrite` (track above, lined up by source timecode).

q: Fill a marked gap in the timeline with the good part of a longer clip by changing its speed.
a:
1. Open the clip in the Source monitor (double-click it in the Media Pool) and mark the part you want: I (`markers.markIn`) at its start, O (`markers.markOut`) at its end.
2. On the timeline, mark the gap: In at its first frame, Out at its last.
3. Target the track it should land on in the track headers.
4. Press Shift+F11 (`edit.fitToFill`). Revolution changes the clip's speed so the whole marked source fills the timeline In to Out. Fit to Fill needs both timeline marks; it's one undo step.
Trade-off: a big speed change shows (fast motion or stutter); if the shot only needs to be a little longer, trimming may look better.

q: swap a take for another one and keep the edit the same length
a: Open the new take in the Source monitor, park its frame you want to line up, put the timeline playhead over the clip to swap (on the destination track) and press F11 (`edit.replace`). The Source monitor frame lands on the playhead and the new clip is as long as the old one, or shorter if its media runs out, so nothing else in the edit moves.

q: Put a cutaway over the interview with one key, using the Resolve keys.
a: Open the cutaway in the Source monitor with its In and Out, park the playhead (or set a timeline In) where it should start and press F12 (`edit.placeOnTop`). It overwrites onto the track above the highest one that has a clip at that point, adding a track when needed, so the interview underneath stays as it is.

q: Why did my F10 edit land at a different spot than the playhead?
a: Because the timeline has an In mark. The Resolve edits use the record point: the timeline In mark when there is one, otherwise the playhead. Clear the timeline marks (Alt+X, `markers.clearInOut`) and the edit goes to the playhead.

q: How do I add a Media Pool clip to the timeline from the control channel without loading it in the Source monitor?
a: Pass the clip's project item id as the optional `clip` parameter, for example run `edit.append` with `{"clip": <item id>}`. Every Resolve edit command (`edit.insert`, `edit.overwrite`, `edit.replace`, `edit.placeOnTop`, `edit.append`, `edit.rippleOverwrite`, `edit.fitToFill`, `edit.smartInsert`, `edit.closeUp`, `edit.sourceOverwrite`) takes it; without it they use the Source monitor's clip.

q: Exchange a shot for a longer alternative and let the rest of the timeline slide to fit.
a: Load the alternative in the Source monitor, put the playhead over the shot to exchange and press Shift+F10 (`edit.rippleOverwrite`). It swaps that clip for the whole source and moves everything after it by the difference in length, so nothing is covered and no gap is left. Use F11 (`edit.replace`) instead when the edit's length must stay the same.

q: My cameras have matching timecode. How do I lay the second angle over the first in sync?
a: Put the playhead over the first camera's clip, load the second angle as the source and run `edit.sourceOverwrite` (on the Cut page, the Source Overwrite button). It puts the source on the track above so its source timecode meets the timecode of the clip under the playhead. If the two recordings' timecodes don't overlap it stops with a message instead of guessing.

q: So how do I go full screen now?
a: In the Resolve key preset full screen moved to Ctrl and the backtick key, since F11 is Replace there.

context.q: why does F11 replace clips with the Resolve keys
context.a: In the Resolve key preset F11 runs Replace (edit.replace), as in Resolve.
